You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

===== task_94595684_block_fill_noise_rule
ARC task-94595684 (demo-confirmed): uniform-background grid contains a few solid rectangular color blocks plus scattered single noise cells (any color incl. 0). Rule: fill each block's full bounding rectangle with the block color (fixes holes/dents); every other cell (all noise singles) becomes the background color. Detect blocks as maximal solid rectangles (>=2 rows and >=2 cols of one color).
===== task_94595684_noise_fill_rule
ARC task-94595684 (solved after 3 wrong attempts): background = most common color; shapes = large 4-connected clusters. Rule: every isolated noise single-cell INSIDE a shape's bounding box is filled with the shape's color (ALL of them, even if the box has several gaps or two gaps share a row/column); every noise single outside all shape bounding boxes is ERASED to background. KEY LESSON: always apply the erase step — two failed attempts only filled holes and left stray noise singles untouched in the submitted grid; verify the submitted grid matches the stated rule cell-by-cell. Earlier 'single-gap completion / adjacency-only' variants were WRONG.
===== task_94595684_noise_hole_rule
ARC task-94595684 (solved, 2 wrong): grid = uniform background + solid rectangular blocks + scattered single noise cells. Rule: for each cell whose 4-neighbors all differ from it (isolated noise cell): if it touches a non-background connected block on >=2 orthogonal sides (2 neighbors of same color in the SAME component), it takes that block's color (hole filled); otherwise it becomes background. Exclude background from fill candidates (it forms one giant component and would otherwise win ties). Key demo evidence: noise cell touching a block on only ONE side becomes background, not block color.
===== task_94595684_noise_removal
ARC task-94595684 SOLVED (noise removal, validated): grid of large solid same-color regions on a dominant background, plus scattered single-cell 'noise' pixels of other colors (some inside the regions). Rule: every connected component of size 1 is replaced by the majority color among its 4-neighbors; larger components unchanged. One demo request confirmed it. General tactic: when a grid is mostly a few big uniform blocks plus many isolated single pixels, first hypothesis = remove isolated pixels to dominant neighbor color.
===== task_94595684_noise_removal_rule
ARC task-94595684 SOLVED rule (noise removal): grid = colored rectangle shapes on uniform background; scattered single 'noise' cells of other colors. Output = input with each noise cell replaced by the MAJORITY color of its 4-neighbors (background if mostly background; shape color only if the noise is interior/fully surrounded by the shape, e.g. demo (25,3)=6 inside 8-shape -> 8). IMPORTANT edge case: a noise cell merely touching/corner-adjacent to a shape still becomes BACKGROUND, not shape color (test (11,17)=8 next to 7-shape -> 6). Method that worked: exact diff of demo input/output to confirm rule, then programmatic application.

These memories conflict somewhat. Latest/best: majority-neighbor rule? Two say "noise single outside bounding box erased to background; inside bounding box filled with shape color" — that was the "block_fill_noise_rule" and "noise_fill_rule" (solved after 3 wrong). And "noise_hole_rule": fill if touching block on >=2 sides with same color, else background. And two "majority neighbor" rules — but those contradict the edge case: a noise cell touching a shape on one side becomes background.

Wait, they conflict: noise_fill_rule says fill ALL noise singles inside the bounding box. noise_hole_rule says fill only if touching on >=2 sides. noise_removal_rule says majority of 4-neighbors. These all coincide with "majority of 4-neighbors" in most cases: inside bounding box noise cell typically touches shape on >=2 sides... actually a hole inside a rectangle touches shape on 2-4 sides → majority = shape color. Outside noise touches shape on ≤1 side → majority = background. So majority-neighbor rule is consistent and simplest. Apply: for each cell not equal to background (9)... wait background is 9 here. Noise cells are scattered 2s and the 4s shape. The 4s block is a component of size>1, keep. Interior 2s inside the 4s shape: neighbors mostly 4s → become 4? Hmm, but "block_fill_noise_rule" says fill block's bounding rectangle with block color. Interior 2s at (16,7),(16,9),(15,7)... Let's just apply majority-neighbor rule.

Check which memory is latest. Order in list: block_fill_noise_rule, noise_fill_rule, noise_hole_rule, noise_removal, noise_removal_rule. The two "SOLVED" majority-neighbor ones came earlier probably. Let me just compute with majority-neighbor and inspect the shape cells.

Actually noise_fill_rule explicitly says fill ALL noise singles inside shape's bounding box even if gaps share row/col, and erase outside ones — that was after 3 wrong attempts and is the most refined. Under majority-neighbor, a noise single inside bounding box with two gaps sharing row/col... e.g. cell with neighbors (left=shape,right=shape,up=bg,down=bg) → tie 2-2. noise_fill says fill with shape color. Majority rule ambiguous on tie → prefer shape color. And a hole adjacent to nothing? Inside bounding box it must touch something.

Plan: background 9, shape color 4. Compute: for each cell not 9 and not part of the 4-block component: if inside bounding box of 4-component → 4; else → 9. Cells equal to 9 stay 9 (background). Cells in 4-block stay 4.
